entries.title: Coinbase Derivatives margin filing states the exchange intends to permit payment stablecoins as margin if the SEC, CFTC or Federal Reserve Board amend their rules
entries.facts: The SEC published Federal Register document 2026-23653 on 2026-11-20, a notice of filing and immediate effectiveness of a Coinbase Derivatives, LLC proposed rule change relating to customer margin requirements for security futures products, Release No. 34-106923, File No. SR-COIN-2026-003, at 91 FR 75421 to 75424. The notice states the change became effective on November 4, 2026, that comments are due on or before December 11, 2026, and that the Commission may summarily abrogate the change within 60 days of effectiveness. The filing adopts Chapter 12 of the exchange rulebook, including Rule 1215 on customer margin, under which the margin requirement for a long or short position shall not be less than 15.05 percent, and is made under Rule 19b-7 because it sets higher margin levels. Rule 1215(c) identifies the types of assets a security futures intermediary may accept from a customer as margin, which the notice limits to deposits of cash, margin securities subject to specified restrictions and further categories, with language to accommodate other assets that may be permitted under applicable CFTC and SEC regulations in the future. The notice states that if the SEC, the CFTC or the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System amend SEC Rule 242.404, CFTC Regulation 41.46 or Regulation T, respectively, or otherwise provide exemptive or interpretive relief, the Exchange intends to permit Participant Firms and Clearing Firms to collect payment stablecoins as margin. The filing was made concurrently with a CFTC certification filed November 3, 2026 and withdraws the earlier SR-COIN-2026-001 filing.
entries.relevant_to: crypto derivatives venues, security futures intermediaries, clearing firms, stablecoin issuers

entries.title: SEC sues eight entities over fake crypto asset trading platforms it says took more than $37 million from US investors
entries.facts: SEC Litigation Release No. 26690, dated November 19, 2026, reports the filing of SEC v. Advisor WeChat Capital et al., No. 26-cv-06302, in the United States District Court for the District of Colorado on November 19, 2026. The eight defendant entities are Advisor WeChat Capital, Tech Brokerage Asset Alliance Ltd., HB Wealth Advisors, IdeaCrypto Exchange LLC, Convergent Wealth Advisors Inc., RealSimple Crypto Exchange Inc., Associated Wealth Advisors Ltd. and Essential Crypto Exchange. All eight are charged under Section 10(b) of the Exchange Act and Rule 10b-5. Advisor WeChat Capital, HB Wealth Advisors, Convergent Wealth Advisors Inc. and Associated Wealth Advisors Ltd. are also charged under Sections 206(1) and 206(2) of the Advisers Act, and Convergent Wealth Advisors Inc. and Essential Crypto Exchange under Section 207 of the Advisers Act. The release describes paired fake investment advisers and fake crypto asset trading platforms, investors contacted through social media and group chats, conduct from August 2024 through May 2026, and approximately $37 million taken. It states the defendants used fake SEC certificates and filings made with the SEC, FINRA and FinCEN, and that a Form D and two Forms ADV were removed from the SEC website. The SEC seeks permanent injunctions, conduct-based injunctions, disgorgement, prejudgment interest and civil penalties. The companion SEC press release is 2026-115 of the same date.

entries.title: CFTC product filings dated 11/20/2026 show certified binary option event contracts on consumer card spend, app downloads and online sportsbook advertising spend
entries.facts: On the CFTC Trading Organization Products filings listing, 25 rows dated 11/20/2026 were read on page 1. Every one of those rows shows Organization KEX, Type Swap (Binary Option), Status Certified and Category Event, with Subcategory either Financial/Corporate or Sports. The Financial/Corporate rows are Carbon Arc array contracts at filings 68307 down to 68301, covering BigTicket Furniture, Quick Service Restaurants, Gas Station Spend, Streaming Apps, Rideshare Apps, Order Delivery Apps and AI Chat Apps, and paired share and growth index contracts at filings 68300 down to 68286 on TikTok Shop revenue for Fenty Beauty, streaming views for House of the Dragon, Zyn point of sale spend, Primary Dental Care healthcare credit card spend, Costco Wholesale foot traffic, Target credit card spend in the United States, DraftKings Sportsbook Casino app downloads, and Online Sportsbook advertising spend. The Sports rows include filing 68284 on whether the Chicago Blackhawks reach a goal threshold first in New York Rangers at Chicago Blackhawks on November 27, 2026, and filing 68281 on a player record count stat in the Indiana Fevers first home game of the 2027 WNBA regular season. The individual pages for filings 68307 and 68281 each show Organization KEX, Type Swap (Binary Option), Status Certified, Date 2026-11-20 and Category Event, and each carries an associated document titled Request for Confidential Treatment, Detailed Written Justification. The listing and both filing pages print the organization code KEX without a full legal name, and neither page cites a certification rule.

entries.title: SEC obtains a temporary restraining order and asset freeze in an alleged $560 million Ponzi scheme that promised to convert investor funds to crypto assets
entries.facts: SEC press release 2026-116, dated November 20, 2026, states that the SEC charged Backward Hat Capital and its co-founders Phillip Williams and Devin Johnson, together with Traders Point Capital and Joseph Anderson, and named relief defendants it describes as an individual and several entities. The action was filed in the United States District Court for the Southern District of Indiana. The release states the action is to halt an ongoing Ponzi scheme, that approximately $560 million was raised from more than 2,000 investors, and that Williams and Johnson promised that investor funds would be converted to crypto assets and then used to engage in FX arbitrage. The charges are under the antifraud provisions of the Securities Act of 1933 and the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, and Williams and Traders Point Capital are also charged under the Investment Advisers Act of 1940. The SEC obtained a temporary restraining order, an asset freeze and expedited discovery, and seeks a permanent injunction, disgorgement and civil penalties. The release states that parallel actions were brought by the United States Attorney's Office for the Southern District of New York and by the CFTC. No case number is printed on the release.
